3.1.3.1 Recreation
Page 3-11
The Cherokee Foothill Trail Conference will meet and undertake a public information program to inform the public of rules and information by placing strategically located signs.
3.1.4.2 Water Quality
Page 3-13, 3-14
Paragraph four - Siltation of streams due to transmission line construction will be minimized by keeping right-of-way clearing to a minimum. Sedimentation from the proposed spoil and construction yard will be minimized as stated in Exhibit W, subsection 3.1.6.
Paragraph five - The DES states that "the waters involved tend to be naturally acidic and are near the lower end of the optimal range of pH values for aquatic life." This is not in agreement with the "Fishery Resource Evaluation" by Don Archer, Fishery Biologist from the South Carolina Wildlife and Marine Resource Department, which reports pH values of 6.7-7.0 in Howard Creek.
Page 3-14
Paragraph one - Duke Power will maintain a surveillance program and will provide insect control as deemed necessary.
Paragraph two - All necessary steps will be taken so, to comply with the EPA oil spill prevention regulations.
3.1.5 Waste Disposal
Page 3-14
It is stated that rock excavated from the tunnels and powerhouse area would be used in the dam or crushed and used as temporary project roads or used as a filler material. Duke proposes to use approximately 400,000 cubic yards of rock excavated from underground tunnels to construct an underwater weir in the Whitewater arm of Lake Jocassee downstream of the Bad Creek discharge. Physical modeling studies have shown that such a weir, extending to within 60 ft. of full pool surface, will reduce the potential for disruption of stratification by discharge water (see "Effects of Bad Creek Pumped Storage om Stratification in Lake Jocassed' by Billy L. Edge, which was mailed to FPC on 26 Aug. 1975). This weir would also extend up through the suitable trout habitat in Lake Jocassee, and thus possibly reduce the number of trout in the immediate vicinity of the intake (see comments on Sect. 9.2). See Exhibit W, Figure 1.4-1, Amendment 1.
Although the Foothills Trail Conference may undertake a sign program, the Applicant would assume primary responsibility to ensure the adequacy of the program pursuant to its commitments in Exhibit R.
